text: Can you describe exactly how your cough feels, and does it produce any mucus? If so, what color is the mucus and how much do you cough up? REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hyperinflation of the lungs, flattened diaphragm, no acute infiltrates.

speaker: Doctor
text: That chest X-ray suggests air trapping, which is often seen in obstructive lung diseases. Do you experience wheezing when you breathe out, and does your cough worsen at night or after exposure to cold air? REQUEST TEST: Spirometry with bronchodilator challenge.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD). The combination of hyperinflated lungs on X-ray, reduced FEV1/FVC ratio on spirometry, and your symptoms is classic for COPD. Do you have a significant history of smoking, or were you exposed to significant dust or fumes in the past?
